The separation between o- and e-rays is given by \(\Delta x = f \cdot 2\left(\arcsin(n_o/2) - \arcsin(n_e/2)\right)\) with \(f = 1\ \text{m}\). Using typical indices for calcite (\(n_o = 1.658\), \(n_e = 1.486\)), \(\Delta x = 0.2796\ \text{m}\). The line dispersion of the spectrometer is \(d\lambda/dx = d/(f m)\) with \(d = 1/(3937)\ \text{cm}\), \(f = 50\ \text{cm}\), \(m=1\), giving \(50.8\ \text{Å/mm}\). For the camera, the defocus blur diameter is \(d = D/200\); setting geometric blur equal to diffraction blur (\(2.44\lambda f/D\)) and using \(\lambda = 500\ \text{nm}\) yields \(D = \sqrt{2.44\lambda u} = 1.10\ \text{cm}\). The coherent area at distance \(10\ \text{m}\) from a \(1\ \text{cm}\) diameter source is \((\lambda R/D)^2\) with \(\lambda=500\ \text{nm}\), giving \(0.25\ \text{mm}^2\).

ANSWER: 0.2796,50.8,1.10,0.25
